item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Yellow Warning - Wind - In Effect |

High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Parks and forests will likely sustain some damage. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. item.title: BE ALERT - ORANGE WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Orange Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to: - Snow - Blowing snow - Wind A significant, long duration snowfall event continues with total snowfall accumulations of 40 to 60 cm expected by Sunday morning. Heavy snow will continue through the day and into tonight before gradually tapering off on Sunday. In addition to the snowfall, strong northerly winds with gusts up to 70 km/h will continue until Sunday. These winds, combined with falling snow, will result in significantly reduced visibility at times in snow and blowing snow. Winds will gradually ease through the day Sunday. Travel will likely be very hazardous. Road closures are possible. Roofs are at an increased risk of collapse under the weight of snow. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

| Extreme - extraordinary threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WIND - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Yellow Warning - Wind - In Effect |

Strong wind gusts expected. What: Strong westerly to northwesterly winds gusting up to 100 km/h. When: Late this afternoon through Sunday. Additional information: A low pressure system tracking across Hudson Bay will bring strong wind gusts to the region. Southwesterly winds will gradually strengthen from west to east beginning this afternoon. The winds will then shift to westerly and northwesterly, with the peak winds expected overnight through Sunday morning. Winds will begin to diminish Sunday afternoon. Local utility outages are possible. Some property damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using ONStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Future - act in near future

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

A significant fall storm will continue to impact northern Manitoba and the Kivalliq today and will persist through the weekend. Where: Churchill and Arviat What: Hazardous winter conditions including: Snow with total amounts of 10 to 25 cm Severe wind gusts possibly exceeding 110 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm. When: Beginning Saturday morning and tapering off Sunday afternoon. Remarks: Precipitation will begin in this area today as rain or freezing rain before transitioning to snow and blowing snow this evening and overnight. Very strong winds will occur also, with gusts up to a possibly 100 to 110 km/h, with drastically reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Snow and winds will gradually taper off Sunday afternoon. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are likely. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

A significant fall storm will continue to impact northern Manitoba today and will persist through the weekend. Where: Areas of northern Manitoba, including, Pukatawagan, Lynn Lake, Brochet, and Tadoule Lake. What: Hazardous winter conditions including: Heavy snow with total amounts of 20 to 40 cm. Severe wind gusts exceeding 90 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Freezing rain with total amounts of 5 to 10 mm. Heavy rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm. When: Rain and freezing rain developed overnight over northern Manitoba. This will transition to snow throughout the day before tapering off Sunday afternoon. Winds will strengthen throughout the day with gusts up to 90 km/h in areas closer to the Nunavut border and will taper off Sunday afternoon and evening. Visibilities will be drastically reduced in blowing snow this afternoon and evening when falling snow and strong winds combine. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Property damage is possible. Property or tree damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

item.title: ACORN Annual Conference & Trade Show
item.description:
ACORN Annual Conference & Trade Show slmacneil Fri, 10/23/2026 - 15:16

Groundwork: From Soil to Sustenance

From building healthy soils and managing pests and disease to exploring new crops, production methods, and ways to make a farm more resilient, Groundwork brings together the knowledge and lived experience that help farms thrive.

Join ACORN for two days of practical learning, conversation, and connection with fellow farmers and growers from across Atlantic Canada.

Whether you’re a seasoned farmer, just getting started, exploring more ecological ways to grow, or simply curious about where our food comes from, you're welcome at the table.

Mark your calendars for February 15-16, 2027, and prepare to gather in Moncton, New Brunswick, for another high-impact two-day event!

Ticket Sales, along with venue details, will go live soon - stay tuned.
 

February 15, 2027 9:00 am to February 16, 2027 4:00 pm

item.title: Province celebrates and invests in community organizations
item.description:
Province celebrates and invests in community organizations jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/23/2026 - 14:59

Today, Minister for Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson wrapped up a week of community celebrations in which he recognized community organizations, commended volunteers, and highlighted investments made through the Rural Growth Initiative (RGI).

"Strong communities are built by people who step up, volunteer, and work together to make life better for their neighbours. Through the Rural Growth Initiative, we are helping local organizations strengthen the places where Islanders gather, learn, stay active, and support one another. These investments are making a real difference in communities across Prince Edward Island, helping them remain vibrant, resilient, and strong for generations to come." 

- Premier Rob Lantz. 

This fiscal year, $6.8 million has been invested in 85 projects around the province, including BGC Montague, supporting the creation of a youth centre that will provide youth programming, leadership development, recreation, and food security supports; the facility upgrades to the West Prince Curling Club, enabling them to host national and regional championships which attract visitors and generate economic activity; and the New Glasgow Rural Community Fire Company Purchasing new bunker gear and portable radios to improve firefighter safety and emergency response capacity.

"The strength of rural Prince Edward Island has always come from the people. Through the Rural Growth Initiative, we are supporting local organizations that provide gathering spaces, recreational opportunities, tourism experiences, emergency services, and community programs that improve the quality of life for those rural Islanders," said Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson. "These projects reflect the dedication of volunteers and community leaders who continue to invest their time and energy into creating vibrant, inclusive and resilient communities."

RGI supports municipalities and non-profit organizations in delivering community infrastructure and capacity-building projects, including upgrades to community spaces, fire halls, and initiatives that strengthen local services and amenities across rural Prince Edward Island. Since 2019, the Government of Prince Edward Island has invested more than $45.6 million on 878 projects across the three counties through RGI.

More information about the Rural Growth Initiative can be found on the provincial website.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
